title: Avro Lancaster JA964
memorial_details: The memorial is a black and white photograph of aircrew in front of a Lancaster, mounted under clear plastic, with crew details in white print. It is about 125 mm high and 180 mm wide, on paper, and its condition is good. It hangs in All Saints' Church, Rampton Road, Longstanton. All Saints' is the custodian. The church is Grade I listed.
inscription: REMEMBERING THE 70TH ANNIVERSARY OF LANCASTER JA964 OF 7 SQUADRON SHOT/ DOWN BY A NIGHT FIGHTER ON 22ND MARCH 1944 RETURNING FROM FRANKFURT/ FG OFF J H WYBORN/ FLT SGT J LAMBERT RAAF/ FLT SGT G E HAMILTON RNZAF/ SGT A E BULLIVANT

sources.title: Lest We Forget: Lancaster JA964 and Flight Sergeant Jack Lambert

narrative:
Lancaster III JA964, marked MG-P, took off from Oakington at 18:58 on 22 March 1944 to bomb Frankfurt. It flew with 7 Squadron, 8 Group. The raid that night involved 816 aircraft, and 33 were lost. Nothing was heard from JA964 after take-off, and it did not return.

Post-war enquiries established that the aircraft had been shot down. The memorial in Longstanton says a night fighter did it. The pilot, Flying Officer Kenneth Hinde, said in 1945 that the Lancaster was attacked ten minutes before the target and again two minutes later, which set the port inner engine on fire. He ordered the crew out at about 16,000 feet and put the crash half way between Frankfurt and Saarbrucken. The bomb aimer, Flight Sergeant Harry McMaster, said he baled out at 19,000 feet with the controls useless and a fire in the port engine. He put the crash 10 miles east of a place he gave as 'Jaoberstein', east of Trier. The two accounts place the crash in different spots, and no source here settles which is right.

Four men died: Flying Officer John Henry Wyborn (navigator, 28), Flight Sergeant Jack Lambert (wireless operator/air gunner, 22, RAAF), Flight Sergeant Gordon Eben Hamilton (rear gunner, 20, RNZAF) and Sergeant Albert Edward Bullivant (mid-upper gunner, 20). All four are buried at Rheinberg War Cemetery. Three survived as prisoners of war: Hinde, Sergeant Albert Ivon Love (flight engineer) and McMaster. Hinde and McMaster were released by the Russians.

external_narratives.summary: Local history page on the church: Grade I listed, nave roof collapse in the early 2000s, closure for about five years, Friends of All Saints' Church formed, reopened 30 September 2007.

community_connection: All Saints' holds the 7 Squadron Memorial Window, dedicated on 17 August 1992, and the squadron's Book of Remembrance, which lists 1,011 Second World War dead. The 7 Squadron Association holds its Remembrance Day service there each autumn. IBCC also lists a window and Roll of Honour at All Saints' in its entry for Sergeant Bullivant. The church was closed for about five years after its nave roof collapsed and reopened on 30 September 2007.
